excluded_seen: The look (look.py here, step 4h): step 4g's sixteen runs on side 2,048 from starts 18001 to 18108, read with a block's past in view. Every claim here was read off it, and reference.json holds its rules.

The sizing look (sizing.py here, exploratory): step 4d's kept runs on side 1,024 from starts 15001 to 15008 through this study's measures, four starts to learn from and four to try on, with the look's rules tried and run on there. Every bound here was drawn from it and from the look. It ran no world.
Steps 4d, 4e and 4g ran these two worlds on sides 1,024 and 2,048 from starts 15001 to 15008, 16001 to 16108 and 18001 to 18108, and read them with nothing of a block's past in view.
No start from 19001 on has been generated or run.
body.not_tested: A claim about a chance is not tested where fewer than 200 blocks stand behind a chance it compares. A claim about a rule run on through blocks of some size is not tested where more than 0.2 of neighbouring blocks of that size have different leaders when the rule is started, on the world's trial starts. And no claim is tested without a number to judge.

readings.as it is: the leader, and how many of the eight neighbours each species leads
readings.with how long in view: the same, and for how many ticks running the block has had its leader, up to 8

A, a block's past.drawn from: the look (side 2,048): with four rival neighbours a block of 8 that has had its leader one tick changes hands 6.2 and 7.0 times as often as one that has had it 16 ticks or more (still, busy), a block of 16 7.9 and 8.1 times; how long, up to 8 ticks, removes 7% to 11% of the plain rule's surprise at blocks of 4 to 16. Step 4d's runs on side 1,024 give the same: 6.2 and 7.0, 7.9 and 8.1; 7% to 11%.

B, the top of the table.drawn from: the look: a lead of 16 ticks or more at five rival neighbours changes hands 0.96 and 1.00 times as often at blocks of 16 as at blocks of 8, where the rule as it is gives 0.85 and 0.87. On side 1,024: 0.93 and 0.97, 0.84 and 0.87; and the rule as it is at blocks of 8, made from its own mix of young and old leads and the chances of blocks of 16, comes out at 0.99 of what it is in both worlds. The still world's old leads do fall a little: this is the bound most likely to be missed.

C, along the walls.drawn from: the look: at three rival neighbours an old lead changes hands 0.38 and 0.32 times as often at blocks of 16 as at 8, a lead of one tick 0.75 and 0.67 times; an old lead at four 0.75 and 0.80 times. On side 1,024: 0.38 and 0.40, 0.77 and 0.71, 0.76 and 0.80; a fifth of the plain rule's fall at three is the mix; and the remembering rule from blocks of 4 has 6.4% to 6.6% and 5.2% to 5.4% more surprise at blocks of 8, which is 0.75 and 0.92 to 0.96 of what the plain rule has.

D, run on.drawn from: the look: 0.73 and 0.77 of the plain rule's blocks amiss at blocks of 8, 0.80 and 0.89 at 16; walls kept 0.86 and 0.89 by the plain rule at blocks of 8, 0.89 and 0.93 at 16, and 1.01 to 1.07 by the remembering one; going back in 0.26 and 0.27 of changes of hands in the world at blocks of 8, 0.25 and 0.24 at 16, within 0.03 of that in the remembering rule's world and 0.3 to 0.45 of it in the plain rule's. On side 1,024, from four trial starts each way: 0.72 and 0.77 to 0.78, 0.82 and 0.90 to 0.91; plain walls 0.84 to 0.90 at blocks of 8 and 0.88 to 0.94 at 16, where one way and the other differ by up to 0.04; remembering walls 1.00 to 1.07; going back within 0.01 to 0.03. The walls at blocks of 16 are what moves most between one choice of starts and another, so their bounds are the widest.

E, the ladder's own test.drawn from: the look: the remembering rule from the rung below ends amiss in 1.14 and 1.03 times as many blocks as the rung's own at blocks of 8, 1.03 and 0.98 at 16; the plain rule from below in 1.20 and 1.09, 1.15 and 1.13. On side 1,024: 1.13 to 1.14 and 1.03, 1.02 and 0.97 to 1.00; the plain rule pays 0.05 to 0.07 more at blocks of 8 and 0.14 to 0.19 more at 16; and the remembering rule from blocks of 8 ends with 0.84 and 0.87 to 0.91 of the blocks the rung's own plain rule gets amiss at blocks of 16.

R, the look's rules.drawn from: the look's rules tried on step 4d's runs, which the look never saw: as it is they have 0.03% to 0.3% less surprise than the rule learned from four of those starts, and with how long in view 0.5% to 2.8% less, having learned from far more; run on, they end amiss in 0.98 to 1.01 times as many blocks. Step 4g's rule of side 1,024 served on side 2,048 within 0.1%.

X, the anchor.drawn from: step 4g's registered bounds for the same two numbers, which held there (2.8% and 3.0%; 0.54 and 0.46). On side 1,024 here: 2.3% to 2.7%; 0.47 to 0.54.

what a claim stands on.drawn from: steps 4e and 4g: a run-on is read only where at most a fifth of neighbouring blocks differ when the rule is started (0.16 to 0.18 at every rung at its matched age). The fewest blocks behind a chance any claim compares were 318 in step 4d's eight starts; the registered run has sixteen.

body.statement: Two worlds of territories are read through blocks of 4, 8 and 16, each on the square clock over the generations that match it, from sixteen fresh starts. How long a block has had its leader says what it does next (A). With that in view the top of the coarse rule's table is the same from blocks of 8 to 16, and the fall of the rule as it is there is the mix of young and old leads (B); along the walls the table still changes at every age of the lead, and one tick ahead the remembering rule changes from rung to rung nearly as much as the plain one (C). Run on by itself, the rule with how long in view ends with fewer blocks amiss, does not lose walls, and goes back as often as the world does (D); and learned one rung down it runs a rung on nearly as well as the rung's own, where the plain rule from below pays (E). The rules the look learned on another grid serve here unchanged (R), and with nothing of the past in view these are the worlds of steps 4e and 4g (X).
